learning_outcomes.text: Have knowledge and understanding to develop, execute, and manage engineering projects adhering to professional best practices, regulations, and norms.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to the analysis of product, process, and method engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
The ability to perform bibliographic searches, use databases and other sources of information.
Awareness of all the implications of engineering practice.
Function effectively both individually and in a team.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of business and project management practices, as well as risk management and control, and understand their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess competencies usually demonstrated through the development and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Knowledge and ability to apply current legislation as well as mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards in the field of mechanical engineering.
Knowledge and ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions, and to apply environmental and sustainability technologies.

syllabus_topics: Engineering projects. Competencies of the mechanical engineer. Types of documents signed by an engineer and their implications.
Selection, adjustment, and tuning of machinery and mechanical elements. Mechanical installations.
Documentation, Standardization, and regulation. Industry Law. Technical regulations.
Safety and hygiene. Machinery Safety Directive.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment activities (including assignments, exercises, practicals, conference/seminar participation, project work)

assessment_rules: To pass the course (ordinary or extraordinary sitting): a minimum grade of 40% must be obtained in both the Final Exam and the Project Work. Attendance at seminars is required, or, failing that, completion of a substitute assignment.
